newsitem.title: USA: Top aide to Wisconsin governor says he resigns.
newsitem.headline: Top aide to Wisconsin governor says he resigns.

text.p: James Klauser, the top aide to Wisconsin Gov. Tommy Thompson, announced on Monday he will resign from state government effective December 6.
Klauser said he was considering various options, including acedemia or returning to a former law practice, according to Kevin Keane, Thompson's spokesman.
"He said it was time. He's been here for 10 years and he wanted to be refreshed," Keane said, referring to comments Klauser made Monday during a joint news conference in Madison with Thompson.

As secretary of the Wisconsin Department of Administration since 1987, Klauser has been in charge of the state's budget and bond issuance. In addition, he was a member of state boards, commissions and committees.
A local newspaper reported that Mark Bugher, the state's revenue head, would succeed Klauser. But Keane said Thompson would not announce a decision until later this week or early next week.
